panels.visual: Dionysus (young, long dark curls, ivy crown, leopard skin) laughing among grapevines, a cup of wine in one hand and a smiling theatre mask in the other
panels.caption: Dionysus was the Greek god of wine, wild parties, and pretending to be someone else.

panels.visual: A crowd of Athenians in spring carrying a wooden statue of Dionysus through the streets with music, ivy garlands and dancing
panels.caption: Every spring Athens held a huge festival for him, the City Dionysia.

panels.visual: A chorus of men in masks singing and dancing round an altar on a flat earth circle at the foot of a hill, people sitting on the grassy slope above
panels.caption: Choruses sang and danced for him on this slope. Then one singer stepped out and played a character. Theatre was born.

panels.visual: The finished stone Theatre of Dionysus on the south slope of the Acropolis, rows of seats packed with about 16,000 people
panels.caption: Later the hillside got stone seats for about sixteen thousand people.

panels.visual: Three playwrights side by side as in a poster: Aeschylus (bald, old soldier), Sophocles (handsome, calm), Euripides (thoughtful, beard, scroll)
panels.caption: Three great writers of tragedy had their plays first performed here: Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides.

panels.visual: Judges dropping voting tablets into an urn while three playwrights wait nervously; one is crowned with ivy
panels.caption: It was a contest. Judges voted, and the winner got an ivy crown.

panels.visual: Backstage: a bearded male actor holding up a sad woman's mask, about to put it on, wearing a long queen's robe
panels.caption: All the actors were men. Even when they played queens, they wore masks.

panels.visual: On stage, the masked actor playing Queen Hecuba of Troy, kneeling and grieving, burning city painted behind; the audience weeping
panels.caption: In Euripides' play Hecuba, a man in a mask played the grieving Queen of Troy, and thousands cried.

panels.visual: The front row of marble seats with names carved into them, important men in fine robes sitting in them
panels.caption: The front row was marble seats for VIPs.

panels.visual: Close-up of the grand central marble throne with carved lion's paws for feet and decorations, a priest of Dionysus in robes sitting on it
panels.caption: The best seat, right in the middle, was for the priest of Dionysus. Look: lion's paws for feet.

panels.visual: Today: the ruined theatre on the slope, tourists among the marble thrones, the Acropolis above
panels.caption: The theatre is still here, and so are the thrones.

panels.visual: Two girls sitting in the front row next to the priest's throne, Glauka the owl perched on its arm
panels.caption: Find the priest's throne. Best view in the house.

speech.speaker: Glauka
speech.text: Try not to cry at the play.
